run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three requested queries were executed and each returned zero on the literal field names asked for, because each index uses a different severity/timestamp schema. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no 'level' field (its mapping is @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword); term level=ERROR returned 0 and the severity-keyed re-run, term severity=ERROR, also returned 0 with an empty severity terms bucket, because that index returned zero documents at all inside the readable window 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z-2026-11-21T09:05:15Z even though the index listing reports 16 stored documents. So index a's ERROR count inside the window is 0, but its count outside the window is unobservable here. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has no 'level' field; its severity field is the integer severity_num (mapping: @timestamp date, msg text, severity_num integer, svc keyword). terms level=[ERROR,FATAL] returned 0; the correct query terms severity_num=[5,6] returned 8 documents in the window (6 with severity_num=5, 2 with severity_num=6), and an independent msg phrase filter on "[ERROR]"/"[FATAL]" also returned 8, confirming 5=ERROR and 6=FATAL. (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no @timestamp field (mapping: ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), so the @timestamp range returned 0 and no time filter could be applied by the search tool; re-running as a lexical range on the keyword field ingest_ts for today (2026-11-21, gte 2026-11-21T00:00:00, lte 2026-11-21T23:59:59) plus term level=ERROR returned 7. For reference, the whole index contains 12 level=ERROR documents (7 dated 2026-11-21, 5 dated 2026-11-20) out of 16 documents. This is a data-shape/count investigation, not a fault diagnosis; no root cause object is asserted.

claims.text: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps only @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); it has no 'level' field.
On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, term level=ERROR returned total 0 over 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z-2026-11-21T09:05:15Z (the search tool also applied its non-removable @timestamp filter to that window).
Re-running on the correct severity field of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, term severity=ERROR, also returned total 0 in the same window, and a terms aggregation on severity returned no buckets at all.

A match_all query with size 0 on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 inside 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z-2026-11-21T09:05:15Z, while the index listing reports docs.count=16 for that index, so its documents carry @timestamp values outside the readable window.
app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has no 'level' field, and terms level=[ERROR,FATAL] returned total 0.

The correct severity query on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, terms severity_num=[5,6], returned 8 documents over 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z-2026-11-21T09:05:15Z, with buckets severity_num=5 doc_count 6 and severity_num=6 doc_count 2.
The full severity_num distribution of app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 in the window is severity_num=3 (5 docs), 5 (6 docs) and 6 (2 docs), total 13 documents.

Sampled documents from app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 show severity_num=5 on msg '[ERROR] DB timeout ...', severity_num=6 on msg '[FATAL] Disk full ...', and severity_num=3 on msg '[INFO] healthcheck ...', and a msg phrase filter on "[ERROR]"/"[FATAL]" counted 8 documents, equal to the severity_num=[5,6] count of 8.
app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it has no @timestamp field, and the range query on @timestamp returned total 0 with time_filter applied=false.

Re-running on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 as a lexical range on the keyword field ingest_ts (gte 2026-11-21T00:00:00, lte 2026-11-21T23:59:59) plus term level=ERROR returned total 7, with the by_level aggregation bucket level=ERROR doc_count 7.
app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 contains 12 level=ERROR documents in total (term level=ERROR, no date filter possible), against 16 documents stored in the index.

Sampled app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 documents show ingest_ts as keyword strings without a timezone suffix, e.g. '2026-11-21T08:01:00', with level ERROR ('err today 1-7', 'err yest 1-5') and level INFO ('info today 1-4').

The 16 documents of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 carry @timestamp values that lie entirely outside the authorized window (e.g. earlier than 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z), which is why every query on that index returned 0 in-window; this is inferred from docs.count=16 with 0 in-window matches and was not directly observed, since the search tool cannot query outside the authorized window on a date-mapped @timestamp.

Normalize the three indices' schemas (a single severity field of one type, e.g. level keyword, and one ISO-8601 date field such as @timestamp) so counting by severity and by day does not require per-index field guessing; this is advisory only and out of scope for this read-only run.

gaps: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3's own ERROR count outside the authorized window is unknown: the index reports 16 stored documents but a match_all returned 0 within 2026-11-20T09:05:15Z-2026-11-21T09:05:15Z, and the search tool's non-removable @timestamp filter plus the authorized-window limit prevent reading those documents, so 0 is a window-scoped result, not proof the index has no ERROR entries.
The actual @timestamp values of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3's 16 documents were not observable, so I cannot state which day/period they belong to.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-typed time field (ingest_ts is keyword), so no time filter was applied by the tool; the 'today' scoping relies on a lexical range over keyword strings that carry no timezone, and documents with ingest_ts later than the authorized window end (2026-11-21T09:05:15Z) would still fall inside the literal 2026-11-21 day range used.
Whether index a or index c entries are semantically the same application's logs as index b (svc=order-280) was not verified; only index b exposes an svc label.
next_steps: If index a's own severity counts are actually needed, request an authorized window that covers those documents' @timestamp values, or have the index re-indexed with an ISO date-mapped time field so the window filter can reach them.

Confirm with the log-pipeline owner which severity encoding is authoritative (a: severity keyword values; b: integer severity_num 3/5/6; c: level keyword) before building any cross-index ERROR dashboard.
Consider mapping c's ingest_ts as a date (or adding a date field) so day-bounded ERROR counts are exact and timezone-explicit rather than lexical keyword comparisons.
